answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil identities by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before claiming rewards. A hollow identity must immobilize real value; if linked accounts fake activity, a random audit can forfeit that bond. The attacker pays the opportunity cost of every lock and risks losing it, so adding identities multiplies the cost instead of free influence. An onyx ledger records locks and penalties, while a haven for honest agents is funded by verified work, not account count.
